Would that we learned, my brother, from this blind man how to cry out to God, and let nothing stop us until we obtain what we hope for from Him, especially the salvation of our souls.
Christ's entry into Jerusalem, the cursing of the fig tree, the cleansing of the temple

"Bethphage and Bethany": the two villages nearest to Jerusalem on the south-east side. The priests used to live in "Bethphage" because of its nearness to the temple, and the meaning of its name is "house of figs", because of the abundance of fig trees in it. And "Bethany" means "house of affliction", and in it lived Lazarus and his two sisters, and the Lord visited it often.

"A colt tied": as Christ drew near to Jerusalem, He sent two of His disciples (who represent the ministry of the two Covenants - the Old and the New) to the nearby village, to bring Him a colt to ride on His entry into Jerusalem. "Whereon never man sat": in this is a symbol of the virgin, pure heart that God needs from us, for God does not sit in a heart in which sin sits ... so let us hasten to repent, so that God may find a place for Himself in us ... And it is noticed that St. Matthew, in (Mt 21:7), says that the two disciples brought also the ass (the mother of this colt).
Since the Lord knew what the two disciples would meet when they went, He explained to them and guided them how to act with the owners of the colt; and what the Lord had told them happened exactly.

And this teaches us, beloved, that whoever holds fast to the Lord's commandments and the Church's guidance, the Lord subdues all opposers before him, and gives him grace before everyone with whom he deals...

So are you in fact careful not to move except by God's counsel and in obedience to Him in all your decisions, that you may experience and see how God prepares the way, and opens the closed doors before you?

The two disciples returned with the colt to the Lord, who consented to ride a colt as a symbol of humility and peace, and not a horse as a symbol of pomp and pride ... and so His love brought Him down from the Cherubic chariot to the colt!! As for the casting of garments on the colt, it was its preparation for His sitting on it ... and the symbolic meaning is the acceptance of Christ's headship and kingship, for the taking off of a garment in ancient times meant submission to those of honor ... and likewise many of the common people gathered around the Lord did, by spreading their garments, declaring their acceptance of Christ the King in the procession of His entry into Jerusalem, spreading and carrying olive branches, which symbolize peace, and palm branches, which symbolize victory.

"They that went before, and they that followed": some went before the Lord Christ in His procession, in a reference to the prophets and saints of the Old Testament who preceded His coming, and some followed Him, in a reference to the Apostles and the believers of the New Testament ... and the shout of all carried more than one meaning:
"Hosanna": it means "save us", and they meant that Christ was their awaited hope for their deliverance from the occupying Romans.
"Blessed is He that cometh": a passage from (v. 26) of (Ps 118), and it means that the One who comes is the one anointed by God and according to His will.

"Blessed be the kingdom ... of David": another declaration of hope that the hearts of the crowd were attached to Christ the King, who would restore to them the glories of the kingdom of Israel as in the days of David...
"Hosanna in the highest": that is, the awaited salvation has as its source the heavenly will of God.

My beloved brother ... Christ's entry into Jerusalem riding a colt is a lesson in which the Lord wanted to teach us humility ... was it not possible for Him to ride a horse? But He chose a simple procession, confirming what He had begun from His birth in a manger ... but as for you and me, what do we seek?! And why do we pursue the passing honor of the world?! My God ... teach me to follow Your example, and to learn from You how to be simple and humble in everything.
After a quick tour during which the Lord visited Jerusalem and the temple, He went out again to Bethany to spend the night, He and the Twelve, with Lazarus, Mary and Martha.

entries.section: (2) The cursing of the fig tree

paragraphs.text: "On the morrow": on Monday morning, on His return to Jerusalem, He was hungry, that is, He was hungry for our good works which He expects from us. But what was our state, and the state of the Jewish nation in particular?! It had the outward appearance of faith (the abundance of leaves, as in v. 13), but without fruit, that is, without works.

entries.section: (2) The cursing of the fig tree

paragraphs.text: "For the time of figs was not yet": was it hidden from Christ that it was not the time for the fig to bear fruit?!
Of course Christ knew before going to it that it had no figs ... and therefore we must understand these verses spiritually.

entries.section: (2) The cursing of the fig tree

paragraphs.text: The Lord cursed the fig tree before His disciples, because: "every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire" (Mt 3:10).

This is a clear and strong warning from God to us all ... perhaps we are often like this tree, having the form and outward appearance of righteousness and godliness, and perhaps of service, without our having the real fruit that God hopes for from us ... would that you, my brother, sat in a quiet sitting and called yourself to account ... what if Christ came now and asked me for my fruits, what would I offer Him?!

"His disciples heard it": it shows the disciples' concentration on everything the Lord said. And this concentration and memorizing is the basis of Church tradition, that is, what the Apostles handed down orally to the following generations.

The aim of the visit to Jerusalem was the temple, of course, and when Christ entered it, He took care to cleanse it of the corruption that had attached to it, for merchants, thieves and bribe-takers had spread through it, with blemished sacrifices, and worship had turned into trade, and the house of God had become a market.

"Carry any vessel through the temple": because of the temple's central location in Jerusalem, some used it as a passage to shorten the way, entering by one gate and leaving by another, especially if they were carrying loads in order to save effort, so the Lord forbade them, because this conflicts with the honor of the house of God.

"And He taught": the Lord Jesus was not content with showing zeal and driving out the sellers, but gave teaching and explanation of what He was doing, and of the honor and reverence we must offer to the Church, the house of God, and He described His house as being for prayer and worship, and not a place for gain and profit-seeking, describing those who do that as thieves.

When the scribes and Pharisees saw the strength of Christ's authority in His work and in His teaching, and the people's being moved and their admiration for what He did, they feared Him, and feared for themselves - they being sinners - so feelings of envy, jealousy and anger seized them, and they sought to kill Him.

And in the evening, Christ returned to Bethany, where He would spend the night outside Jerusalem. My beloved brother ... the Church, the house of God and of the angels, David prayed and sang of it, saying: "Holiness becometh Thine house, O Lord, for ever (that is, to eternity)" (Ps 93:5). And how much we need to be an example to our children in teaching them how to respect the house of God ... for reverence, humility and silence during the prayers are among the most important matters to be observed, so that the heart may be occupied with God alone.

entries.section: (4) The withered fig tree and the effectiveness of faith

paragraphs.text: And in the morning, that is, Tuesday, as they passed by, that is, were passing (on their way to Jerusalem), the disciples saw the cursed fig tree dried up from the roots, that is, down to its roots. And Peter was the first to notice that, and remembered yesterday, and addressed his words to Christ, calling Him to look at it!

entries.section: (4) The withered fig tree and the effectiveness of faith

paragraphs.text: "Have faith in God": that is, why do you marvel at what happened?! Where is your faith in God and in His power to do anything, He being the Creator by the Word? And Christ completed His talk with His disciples saying that faith, if it is without doubt, removes mountains, and that everything a man asks in faith according to God's will, he will obtain. But we must pray at all times with this faith, trusting in God's answer at the right time, and according to His goodness, and in what agrees with the way of the salvation of our souls.

My God and my good Savior ... I fear that I am a fig tree bearing nothing but leaves, but without fruit that pleases You. Therefore I ask You to be patient with me in Your longsuffering, and to make me care only for what You ask of me, and free me from my concern for people's opinion of me and my concern for myself and my appearance ... for all I want is for my life to be a sweet fruit in Your holy mouth...

entries.section: (4) The withered fig tree and the effectiveness of faith

paragraphs.text: After Christ had spoken about the answering of prayer, whose basis is faith, He set another condition for the answering of prayer, namely forgiveness for the one who has wronged us, and made clear that our forgiveness of the other is the basis of God's forgiveness of us. And perhaps we remember that after the Lord Christ taught us the Lord's Prayer, which contains many petitions, He commented on not one thing in all of it, except what He said here, namely that the condition of God's forgiveness of us is our forgiveness of the other (see Mt 6:14-15).

entries.section: (5) The authority of the Lord Jesus

paragraphs.text: The cursed fig tree was on Christ's way to Jerusalem, and when He arrived with the disciples at the temple, the chief priests, the scribes and the Pharisees asked Him:
"By what authority doest Thou these things?": a question carrying two meanings of protest:

The first: what Christ did in cleansing the temple, and the fear and envy this stirred in their souls. The second: the authority of Christ's teaching the crowds in the temple; for whoever taught in the temple took a permit for this from the priests and elders...
And the overall meaning of this question is: who are you, that you teach, or drive out the sellers and money-changers and overturn their tables?!

entries.section: (5) The authority of the Lord Jesus

paragraphs.text: Of course, and as was the Lord Christ's custom in His wisdom and His exposing of the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, He answered their question only with a question that caused them confusion ... about the extent of their acknowledgment of John and his mission ... was it from God or a human claim of John's?!

entries.section: (5) The authority of the Lord Jesus

paragraphs.text: St. Mark made clear the bewilderment into which the priests, scribes and elders fell as a result of Christ's question, and they reasoned that their answer would not be logical in any case, but would put them in a predicament before themselves because they had not believed John on the one hand, and before the people on the other hand, because they could not face the crowd by saying that John was an ordinary man.

entries.section: (5) The authority of the Lord Jesus

paragraphs.text: And so the Lord did not give them the opportunity to bring any accusation against Him, or to try to seize Him, for they declared their inability before His wisdom...

Let us learn from the Lord, the source of all wisdom, how to answer the wicked who plot evil against us ... and we have no rescuer in these situations except quick prayer, lifting the heart before we speak, asking God's help.
The opposition to Christ in Jerusalem; His call to humility and giving

The Lord took advantage of the gathering of the people around Him in the temple, and spoke to them with this parable, intending to make clear what God suffered with the Jewish Church in the Old Testament.
"A certain man planted a vineyard": God, the founder, who called His people with great concern and exceeding care.

"Set an hedge ... digged a place for the winefat": that is, He guarded this vineyard with His strong hand, and the place for the winefat means that He prepared it to receive the good and the fruit of the vineyard's produce (that is, Christ the Savior, from the seed of this people, and suffering in the winepress).

"And built a tower": a tower or house for guarding, and it is the temple, and He delivered the people and the temple to the priests and the leaders, in whom He assumed the protection of His people, and gave them authority (went into a far country).

These verses show God's many attempts to visit His people through the successive prophets, and what the wicked people did to them, for there were those who despised His teaching, and those who beat him and wounded his head, that is, broke his head and nearly killed him, and others killed him in fact (like Isaiah) ... and so it was the lot of all generations of the prophets to be scourged and insulted, and the people and their priests forgot that by this they were insulting the owner of the vineyard Himself.

As an expression of the despair of the owner of the vineyard over attempts to reform the husbandmen, he sent his only son, who bears all the Father's authority, that perhaps they would reverence him and fear him and turn back from their evil.

Here the Lord Christ moves us in the parable to His present time, and to what would happen to Him, by the scheming of the wicked priests and scribes, in plotting against Him to kill Him and crucify Him outside the vineyard, that is, outside Jerusalem.

After the death of the Son, and the Jewish nation's continuing in refusing the last call from the Father - redemption - God rejects those who rejected Him and destroys the husbandmen, that is, the obstinate priests, and gives (transfers) the vineyard (the Church) to others (the Gentiles and the priesthood of the New Testament).

"Have ye not read": the accusation became clear and directed by Christ at the chief priests, scribes and elders, that what He said in the parable applies to them ... and He adds that what David said in (Ps 118:22-23), which they know well, applies to them and to Him, for they rejected Him, and He is the head of the corner.
"The head of the corner": that is, the cornerstone, which is the foundation stone at which the corners of the wall meet and which supports them, and it is like the concrete column of our time.

"And they sought to lay hold on Him": the listeners, elders and priests, understood that the parable was against them, and so rage overcame them, so that their decision was to kill Him. But the crowds gathered and loving the Lord's words were the only obstacle to their arresting Him, so they went away with their rage.

Give me, my God, a heart that realizes Your constant call to me, so that it responds to You and does not neglect Your commandments ... remove from it the hardness of the wicked husbandmen, that I may be obedient to You and to Your Church, doing all that I hear and learn.

The enemies gathered together to inform against the Lord Jesus and entrap Him. For the Pharisees are the learned, strict Jews, and they represent the Jewish nation. As for the Herodians, they are the followers of Herod, the representative of the occupying Romans in government. And they asked Him, after praising Him, so that He might lose His caution toward them, about the law of paying taxes to Caesar - the occupier - and in their craftiness, they bound their question with this phrase: "Shall we give, or shall we not give?" to confine His answer to yes or no. If He said yes, they would accuse Him of favoring Caesar and of loyalty to the Romans. And if He said no, they would accuse Him of hostility to Caesar and of inciting against him.
The Lord Christ exposed their deceit and purpose, and surprised them with the question: "Why tempt ye Me?"

And He completed His talk by asking for a penny - a Roman metal coin - and when it was brought, Christ asked a second question about whose were the image and the inscription on the two faces of the coin, and they answered: Caesar's.
Christ answered in His wisdom with an answer that none of them expected, but which disappointed their hopes of seizing Him or complaining against Him...

As for the spiritual meaning of the answer, it is: that we give the spirit its needs, and the body also, that is, that we not fall short in our attitudes and our faithfulness toward our duties in the world, but not at the expense of God and life with Him.

"The Sadducees": they are a Jewish sect who trace themselves to Zadok the high priest in the days of Solomon, and they came to Christ to tempt Him also, and they did not believe in the resurrection of the dead. St. Mark took care to point to their doctrine, so that we may understand the reason for their following question, which is not free of mockery of the resurrection, and reveals their limited material understanding of eternal life.

"Moses wrote": that is, in the legislation of the Law (Deut 25:5-6), that if a married man died before having children, his brother must marry the widow of the deceased, and register the first son in the name of the deceased, so that his name would not vanish from his tribe and his inheritance not be lost.

The Sadducees presented their controversial question with the aim of examining Christ, and of provoking the Pharisees, and of ridiculing the idea of the resurrection, namely: to which of the seven husbands will she be wife?! See the explanation of (Mt 22:

Christ's answer to them came rebuking, as He confronted them with the deviation of their faith, and attributed the reason for that to their turning away from God's law through rational disputation, and their making light of God's strength and power for the resurrection of the dead, and He made clear to them in (v. 25) that there is no bodily marriage in the resurrection, but the bodies will be spiritual and luminous like the bodies of the angels, so there is no need there for multiplying or procreation.

The Lord Christ returns to affirm the doctrine of the resurrection of the dead, and gives proof from the Holy Bible, for He reminds the Sadducees of the conversation that took place between God and Moses on Sinai, at the bush (Ex 3:6, 16), and how God presented Himself to Moses, when He said that He is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it is not reasonable that God would ascribe Himself to the dead, but to the living. And Christ ended His talk as He had begun it with them, that they had deviated from the faith by their rejection of the truth of the resurrection from among the dead.

My beloved God ... the resurrection and eternity are a truth we believe in, but they are often absent from our hearts, so we are occupied with the perishing world, and forget what remains for us ... grant us, Lord, to care for "the things that remain instead of the things that perish, and the eternal instead of the temporal", as the Church teaches us to pray in the Litany of the Departed.

After the Pharisees had asked about tribute, and the Sadducees about the resurrection, it was the turn of the scribes, and one of them asked, having been pleased with the Lord Christ's answer to the Sadducees, by which He rebuked them and silenced them. The question of this scribe was: "Which is the first commandment of all?" that is, what is the commandment that can be considered the most important among the commandments?

The Lord Christ's answer came that God is one and He is the first before all things, and therefore the first commandment is that man love God with all his heart (his emotions), and with all his soul (his spirit), and with all his mind (his intellect), and with all his strength and effort (his ability). As for the second commandment, which is connected with it and completes it, it is man's love for any other man, for all human beings are relatives from one father, Adam, and Eve the one mother; and there is no commandment greater than these two, because they contain within them and outside them everything.

This scribe approved of Christ's answer, and testified to Him of his agreement with what He said, that God must be loved with the whole human being, and that love of the neighbor as oneself is the best sacrifice offered to God of all.
Christ rejoiced at the man's answer, and declared to him that he was not far from salvation.
And this declaration is for us all, for love of God and of man are the most important commandments of Christianity, and whoever strives in them gladdens God's heart.

And St. Mark mentions that Christ received no further questions from the sects of the Jews gathered around Him, and he also hinted that the reason was the comprehensive and decisive answer to everything He was asked about, so no one dared to ask Him again.

entries.section: (5) Christ, son of David or Lord of David

paragraphs.text: "How say the scribes": the Lord Christ here began by taking the initiative with a question about what the scribes and Pharisees teach, that the awaited Christ is the son of David and of his seed. And this question had more than one reason: to make clear the ignorance of the Jewish teachers of the whole truth, and the shortcoming of their understanding, and then to prove His divinity by declaring that He Himself is the Lord of David.

entries.section: (5) Christ, son of David or Lord of David

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ did not ask in order to receive an answer, but asked in order to answer and teach and make clear the following:

That David in (Ps 110:1) prophesies by the Holy Spirit and says: "The Lord said to my Lord", that is, the Father said to the Son: "Sit Thou on My right hand", that is, Yours is all My authority and My power, and I subdue all Your opposers and the kingdom of evil under Your feet, that is, under Your authority; how then can He be the son of David and his Lord at the same time ... and of course, what is meant is that Christ in His Incarnation came from the seed of David and the tribe of Judah, but He is the God worshiped by David, who calls Him: my Lord.
"The common people heard Him": St. Mark shows the difference between the joy of the simple people in Christ's teaching, and the rage of the priests and leaders at His talk.

entries.section: (6) The warning against the scribes and Pharisees

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ gives new teaching to the people which carries within it a rebuke of the scribes, for He warns them against behaving with pride and showiness like the scribes who wear the long robes, which is a long loose garment - like the Arab abaya - out of a desire to be distinguished, and who prefer places crowded with people such as the markets, to appear in them and exchange greetings ... likewise when they are invited to a gathering or a banquet, they take the best, most conspicuous places.

entries.section: (6) The warning against the scribes and Pharisees

paragraphs.text: The Lord also exposes the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, and reveals the sin of their material profit from the service, for they covet the money and inheritance of widows ... and even their prayers are not for God, but for people's praise of them.

Thus, it was necessary for the Lord Christ to reveal to us all the seriousness of the sin of pride, self-love and showiness, and how all this corrupts worship, and makes us, instead of enjoying God, only store up judgment for ourselves by our lack of humility and contrition ... so, my God, make me not care for my honor with those around me, but for You alone, for You are the One who searches and looks into my depths.

"Over against the treasury": that is, the box of the temple, where the people used to bring their offerings. And the expression "beheld how" means in the original Greek "continued to look", and it is a beautiful spiritual expression meaning that God is always looking at the offerings and gifts of His children, which express their love for Him. And the word "how" St. Mark mentioned as an introduction that God looks at the manner and the heart more than the amount and the appearance.

In the midst of the rich who give much, a poor woman came offering two mites, whose value was a farthing, that is, a quarter of the Roman coin at that time, equal to 1/40 of a denarius, and it was the least value and coin that existed ... and despite the smallness of the sum, Christ wanted to give the disciples new teaching, strange to human understanding and measure ... so the Lord considered that what the widow offered was, in God's eyes, more than all the large sums the rich paid, and made clear to them that the woman, though poor, gave God all she had and withheld nothing, while the others gave some of what they had.
And we learn two things here:

The first: that we do not judge anyone in what he offers, even if it is little, for God alone knows the circumstances of the person; perhaps someone who fasted one hour with weak health is better than another who fasted a whole day and in his fasting was careless in resisting his sins.
The second: that we not delay God's rights such as the tithes under the pretext of our financial need ... did not this woman offer all her living?!
Thirteen: signs of the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the world; the necessity of spiritual vigilance. Introduction to the chapter:

This chapter corresponds exactly with (Mt 24), and its events took place on the Tuesday of Holy Week. And it contains prophecies relating to the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 70 A.D. at the hands of Titus the Roman commander (as will come in detail in v. 14), and others relating to the end of time and the second coming of Christ, and we must distinguish between them, and the interweaving of these signs goes back to two reasons:

(1) There was a strong belief among the Jews that the temple would not be ruined and demolished except at the end of the world and its passing away, and consequently the two events (the destruction of the temple and the end of the world) were linked as one event in the disciples' minds.

(2) Whether it is the destruction of Jerusalem and the death of thousands of Jews, or the end of the world, the lesson drawn from both is one, namely preparation by repentance, and therefore Christ's closing talk in this chapter was about preparation (vv. 32-37).

Herod the Great rebuilt the temple in Jerusalem, and made it a splendid building, in the year 15 B.C. And its completion came in the year 64 A.D., and it had stood for about five centuries since the time of Ezra. Herod did not build it in honor of God, but to please the Jews. And Christ's prophecy about it was fulfilled in the year 70 A.D. at the destruction of Jerusalem and the demolition of the temple.

And as Christ was leaving the temple with His disciples, one of the disciples spoke - with pride - of the greatness of the temple's construction and the size of its great stones. So Christ took advantage of this remark to begin directing His talk about the destruction of Jerusalem and the demolition of the temple and its passing away, and in this there is more than one meaning and symbol:
(1) The demolition of the temple: it means the end of the era of animal sacrifices, and the beginning of the age of the Church, whose sacrifice is Christ Himself, and not the blood of goats.

(2) The demolition of the temple: it also means the death of our old man by Baptism, and the resurrection of our new spiritual man. (3) The demolition of the temple: it teaches us not to be dazzled by the glories of the world however great they may appear, because everything on earth has an end, but what is in heaven remains and is eternal.

The Mount of Olives lies east of Jerusalem, and because of its height the whole city can be seen, and the temple clearly as well. And when Christ and the disciples sat down, four of them came to Him, asking about the signs of the happening of what He had spoken of - the demolition of the temple. And St. Matthew adds in (Mt 24:3) that they also asked Him about His second coming and the end of the age, because they considered it one event, as was pointed out in the introduction to this chapter.

As for the Lord Christ, He began His important talk to the disciples by warning them of the appearance of false people who claim to be the Christ, or messengers from Him, and who will be a cause of the straying and destruction of many; so the Church in all her ages must beware of them.

It is noticed that the Lord Christ, in His talk about the signs, did not specify times. And the Church also teaches us the same teaching, not to be occupied with times but with repentance and preparation.

entries.section: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ here tells the disciples of some difficult matters that will meet them and the believers in the period between His ascension and the destruction of Jerusalem, a period full of wars and informing against them, for they will be exposed to trials before the councils and synagogues of the Jews, and because of Him they will be beaten. But all this will be an opportunity for the disciples to bear witness to their faith before those who try them ... and notice that this is exactly what happened in the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7:59), the killing of James and the imprisonment of Peter (Acts 12:2 and 4), and others.

entries.section: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And before the destruction of Jerusalem also, the news of the preaching and the Gospel will be carried to all the surrounding nations, either because the disciples began the work of preaching outside Judea, or because of the Jews who come to Jerusalem in the days of Passover and return to their countries with the news of the preaching, as happened with the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:27-39).
This is in regard to the destruction of Jerusalem, but in regard to the signs of the end of the world, the Christian faith will spread in the world, and many will believe before the second coming.

entries.section: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ here reassures His disciples lest they fear what is coming upon them, for He assures them that the Holy Spirit will never leave them in what they will be exposed to, so they should not worry before the trials and interrogations and not be troubled, because the Holy Spirit Himself will give them wisdom and boldness, so they must obey and speak what the Spirit dictates to them.

entries.section: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And because of the new faith, one house will be divided against itself, so that unbelieving children may kill their fathers who have believed and vice versa, and likewise a brother with his brother.

entries.section: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Believers in every generation await what Christ foretold to His disciples here, for whoever wishes to live in striving to please God and to preach in the name of Christ, Satan will usually raise many enemies around him... But look, my brother, in hope, at the faithful promise of Christ, for whoever endures these afflictions with patience has eternal salvation, indeed compensation for all he suffered (Rev 21:4). So take courage, my friend, before what meets you, for you are in a covenant with the One who promised.

entries.section: (4) The events of the destruction of Jerusalem and the advice to flee

paragraphs.text: "The abomination of desolation": Daniel prophesied in (Dan 9:23-27) that after the lifting up of the Christ, a prince would come who would destroy Jerusalem and the temple, and abolish the sacrifices and the offering. And the word "abomination" means "uncleanness" accompanying this destruction, that is, what Daniel prophesied and Christ confirmed.

For from the year 66 A.D., Jerusalem was exposed to three Roman sieges, which ended in its storming in the year 70 A.D. at the hands of Titus, who demolished many parts of the temple, and entered it with his idols and images, so it was defiled by them, and indeed the offering of sacrifices in the temple was abolished from that time.

"Let him that readeth understand": a phrase Christ added to His words because He knows that the Gospel will be written and preached among the Gentiles. And the Lord Christ warns of the severity and terrors of the events at that time, so He gives the advice that everyone who is in Jerusalem and the surrounding regions at that time should flee to the tops of the mountains to escape the Roman siege.

entries.section: (4) The events of the destruction of Jerusalem and the advice to flee

paragraphs.text: These verses depict the severity and woes of this destruction, and advice for whoever wants to escape with his life from this devastation. Whoever is on the housetop, let him flee quickly and not think of his belongings in the house, for there will be no time to go back and take them. And whoever works in the field, let him not even care to take his garments which he took off during his work. And matters will be very hard on the pregnant women and the nursing mothers who carry children during the flight. And Christ calls them to pray that the circumstances of the flight be easy, for how hard the flight is in winter and the bitter cold.

My beloved brother ... spiritual flight from evil and uncleanness is the goal of all God's children, and Christ here offers you places where you can take refuge, for the mountains point to height and rising above the desires of the world. And taking nothing out of the house means not caring about material hoarding. And not turning back means steadfastness in repentance and leaving the old sins. And prayer is the constant weapon that accompanies us until our flight is complete and we settle with God in His Kingdom ... Amen.

entries.section: (4) The events of the destruction of Jerusalem and the advice to flee

paragraphs.text: Indeed, the tribulation of the destruction of Jerusalem was very great, for Titus destroyed more than one and a quarter million Jews (in the estimate of Josephus the Jewish historian, one million three hundred and fifty thousand Jews) from Jerusalem and its surroundings. And of course, this scale of destruction had not been known before in this region.

entries.section: (4) The events of the destruction of Jerusalem and the advice to flee

paragraphs.text: It is from God's tenderness that He made the days of the siege no more than five months, to give a chance to the elect, that is, the Christians, to escape with their lives.

Note: the explanation of verses 19 (and 20) also applies to the last days, for the persecution of the last time will be severe. But God's love shortens these days for the sake of the escape of everyone who holds fast to his faith.

entries.section: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ warns us of the appearance of false pretenders who claim to be the Christ, and Satan will support them, so they will bring satanic miracles and wonders, in order to confuse the believers into leaving the faith and following these deceivers, and Christ's word is clear: "believe it not" regarding these liars.

And therefore, we must not rush after any current outside the Church and the spirit of the Holy Bible, however great the miracles of these may be, but let the words of the Lord Christ always be with us: "But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things", and we must keep to prayer, humility, deliberation and obedience to the Church, for these are the best guarantee of escape from the tricks of the deceiver.

entries.section: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

paragraphs.text: "But in those days": that is, before the second coming of Christ, and not the destruction of Jerusalem.
"The sun ... the moon": the darkening of the sun and the moon has more than one meaning:
The first: which is the direct meaning, a reference to the end of the material world with its order which God established, and which depends on the sun and the movement of the planets around it.
The second: that because of the appearance of Christ with His mighty light, the sun appears dark in comparison with Him.

The third: which is the symbolic meaning, that is, after the spread of faith in Christ, the heretics distort the concepts of the faith and scatter the simple, so their minds (the sun) and their hearts (the moon) are darkened.
"The stars of heaven shall fall":
Scientifically: this phenomenon has begun to occur, as some great stars have disappeared from the universe.
Spiritually: the falling of many of the believing and famous Christians, like stars, into error, innovations and heresies.

"The powers that are in heaven shall be shaken": perhaps what is meant here is the elements of nature in the visible heaven, which St. Peter mentioned in his second epistle (2 Pet 3:10) "and the elements shall melt with fervent heat".

entries.section: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ describes the scene of His second coming, for as He ascended and a cloud received Him, so He will come also in the clouds with great power and glory, that is, with majesty and power and His divine authority, and with His glory which none can approach, and the cloud usually symbolizes the divine presence as happened in the days of Moses (Ex 13:21-22), and Solomon (1 Kgs 8:10-11), and at the transfiguration also (Mt; 17:5, Mk; 9:7, Lk 9:34). And God sends His angels and gathers His elect, that is, those who believe in His name and have escaped the great tribulation, from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven, that is, all the regions of the earth.

entries.section: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

paragraphs.text: Christ here gives a parable, whose meaning is: just as you can distinguish some matters from their signs, such as the fig tree's blossoming with its leaves, so you know that summer is near, so also when you see all that I have told you, know that the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the world has become very near.

entries.section: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

paragraphs.text: This is what indeed took place in regard to the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 70 A.D., since most of the disciples and believers were alive and witnessed what happened.

And the Lord Christ concludes with an assurance that removes all doubt from His words, when He said that the passing away of heaven and earth is easier to believe than that one word of His should pass away.
My beloved God ... the signs of Your second coming are terrifying and frightening signs. And yet, I continue in my distance from You, occupied with the matters of this perishing world!!
Make me, my God, always remember Your coming in great glory, and gather me, with those whom Your angels gather, into Your embrace ... convert me, Lord, and I shall be converted.

As for the time and hour of Christ's second coming and the end of the world, it is not for anyone to know it or to strive to know it, since God made this hour in His authority alone, and did not declare it even to the angels; and even Christ did not declare it to any of mankind during His Incarnation.

And Christ makes clear the wisdom of hiding this appointed time from mankind, which is constant preparation, watchfulness and spiritual alertness, for if people knew that the time was still far off, their hearts would grow lukewarm and they would leave the life of repentance and preparation (see the comment and explanation at the end of the chapter: Did the Son not know the time and the hour?)

The Lord Christ here gives a parable by which He confirms the necessity of spiritual watchfulness and care for the salvation of the soul, for Christ Himself is God the Lord, the master of the house, who took a far journey, that is, ascended to heaven after the redemption, and left His house, that is, His Church, to His servants who believe in His name, and gave them gifts and authority, besides His commandments, and assigned to each one his work, to serve in His house according to the gifts distributed to them, and charged the porter, that is, the shepherds and priests, to watch and keep spiritual vigil over His servants.
The Lord Christ gives at the end of the parable a commandment, which is: "Watch", and warns us that "ye know not" the time of His coming.

"At even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning": according to Roman timekeeping, the Romans divided the night into four parts, from sunset to sunrise, that is, twelve hours, each part being three hours. And these parts were called elsewhere the first, second, third and fourth watch, and the word watch means a division or part. And the whole fear is that the Son of God will come and find people asleep in their sins, turned away from caring for the salvation of their soul, so there will be escape for no one. And Christ ends His words with the statement that this warning and admonition about the necessity of watching is not for His disciples only, but for all His servants who believe in His name in the whole world.
An important comment on (v. 32): does the Son know the hour of His coming or does He not know it?! And why did He say: "neither the Son, but the Father"?!

The Church teaches us an important principle, which is that any difficult verse in the Holy Bible is not taken alone, but is interpreted in the light of the rest of the texts of the Bible, as we shall follow in our explanation of this verse ... for Christ, as the heavenly Son of God, of course knows the hour, and the following verses prove that:
1) "All things that the Father hath are Mine" (Jn 16:15): so if the Father possesses all knowledge, the Son possesses it also.

2) "I and My Father are one" (Jn 10:30), "I am in the Father, and the Father in Me ... I am in the Father, and the Father in Me" (Jn 14:10, 11), verses that give the same meaning. (Notice the emphasis in the repetition of the last two verses).

(3) How can He be the Creator and not know when His creation ends?! "All things were made by Him; and without Him was not any thing made that was made" (Jn 1:3). (4) How can all judgment be His, and He not know when He judges? "For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son" (Jn 5:22), and also: "And yet if I judge, My judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent Me" (Jn 8:16).

(5) If we take the verse literally, then the Son also withholds knowledge from the Holy Spirit, and this is impossible, "for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God ... Even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God" (1 Cor 2:10-11).

Therefore, what is meant by this verse is: that Christ, as the Son of Man, and as a man representing all mankind, forbids all people to know this hour and to concern themselves with searching into it, and directs us to attend to repentance and the acceptance of His redemption. We can also say: that Christ knows the hour and the time, and the negation here comes to mean non-disclosure. An example: as when the students ask the teacher about the exam questions, and he answers that he does not know, and the not knowing here means not disclosing, since he himself is the one who set the exam.
The Last Supper, the arrest of Christ and His trial

entries.section: (2) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: After St. Mark has dealt with the priests' plot on Wednesday night, he takes us back to the previous Sunday night (Jn 12:1), where the feast was which the Lord Jesus attended in the house of Simon who had been a leper and whom the Lord healed.

"Bethany": it means "house of affliction", and it is a village lying at the foot of the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Lord used to spend the night in it, and to spend the day in Jerusalem throughout the week of the Passion.
"There came a woman": Matthew and Mark also do not mention who this woman is, while St. John confirmed that she was Mary, the sister of Lazarus and Martha (Jn 12:3).
"An alabaster box": a flask.

"Ointment of spikenard": it is the costliest and most fragrant of perfumes in that time, and it was also pure, that is, concentrated. So she broke the box, that is, the neck of the flask, and poured it on Christ's head. And St. John says that she poured it on His feet, which leads us to conclude that she poured the ointment on His head and His feet.

entries.section: (2) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: Because of Mary's action, many of those present were indignant, some of them from among the disciples (Mt 26:

8), and St. John pointed out that the most indignant of them was Judas (Jn 12:4), and they asked within themselves: why this waste, were not the poor more deserving of its costly price, 300 (denarii)?
Note:

To know how high the price of this ointment was, the wage of a laborer for a day was one denarius (Mt 20:2), and if we subtract the days of the Sabbaths on which work was not permitted, the price of the flask of ointment was equal to a laborer's wage for a whole year.

entries.section: (2) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: The people's rebuke and reproach of her increased, so the Lord Christ intervened in her defense, and repelled every attack on her, indeed He reproved those who reproached her and praised her action, making clear: the poor you have with you always, but My days on earth are few ... and He never rejects the feelings of love offered to Him by His children and His beloved.

entries.section: (2) The woman who poured the ointment

paragraphs.text: What Mary did was as though a prophecy from her of Christ's crucifixion and burial, and this is what Christ declared, that it was for the burying. And Christ was not content only to thank her or praise her, but commanded His pure Apostles to record this event in their Gospels when writing and preaching, so that the whole world might know what Mary, the sister of Lazarus, did, and call her blessed ... We learn from this event:
(1) That Mary offered the dearest thing she had to Christ the Lord ... so what do we offer?
(2) This was an offering of thanks to Christ who raised her brother ... do we thank God for His works with us ... and how do we thank Him?

(3) Would that we did not condemn anyone for his action ... for the one we condemn may be praised by God Himself. (4) God does not forget the labor of love, and praises and encourages His children and calls them blessed ... how good is His heart.

"The first day of unleavened bread": it was Thursday, and on it the leaven was removed from the houses. And the Passover lamb was slaughtered between the third and fifth hours in the afternoon, but it was not eaten before sunset, that is, Friday night, and on that day His disciples asked Him: where shall we go and prepare that Thou mayest eat the Passover?

Since Christ did not want to declare the place openly, lest Judas know and report to the priests, and the disciples be exposed to the danger of being arrested, He sent Peter and John, and gave them a sign that they would meet a man bearing a pitcher of water and follow him to the house, then ask the master of the house about the place, and he would show them a place at the top of the house, "a large upper room furnished". And there the two disciples were to prepare the Passover for the Lord and the rest of the disciples. And let us note the following:
(1) The Lord Jesus, and none of His disciples, had a house in Jerusalem, and therefore He used another man's house.
(2) Church tradition tells us that this house is the house of St. Mark, the preacher of all the land of Egypt.
(3) The Lord Jesus used the sign of the "pitcher of water" before the institution of the Eucharist (the sacrament of Communion), in a clear indication that Baptism by water precedes Communion.

In the evening (that is, Friday night), the Lord Christ came with His disciples to the place prepared for eating the Passover. And as they sat down to eat, Christ made an announcement that fell like a thunderbolt on His disciples, namely that one of the Twelve would betray Him, and that he was one of those who eat with Him.

The disciples' feeling changed from joy in celebrating the most splendid of the Jews' feasts to sorrow and bewilderment, and they began to ask aloud, one after another: "Is it I?" And a confirming answer came: yes, it is one of you. And He gave another sign, that the one who betrays Him would dip his hand in the same dish from which Christ eats. And St. John adds in his Gospel (Jn 13:26) that Jesus indeed dipped the sop in the dish and gave it to Judas to eat, as a final silent indication that Judas was His betrayer ... all these calls, hints and warnings had as their purpose Judas' repentance. But the picture shows us how the evil heart that loves money did not respond to God's warnings, despite their clarity and repetition. In addition to that, we find that Judas attended the Passover with everyone although he was determined to betray Christ, but in obvious hypocrisy he took part in this table ... do we do like him at times?!
May the Lord give us a watchful, sensitive heart, quick to respond and to return from the way of evil...

The Lord affirmed that He is going on His way for the redemption of mankind as it was in the prophecies, but this does not excuse Judas from the punishment of his treachery and betrayal, for God did not make Judas betray Him, and He could have been arrested and crucified without Judas having any part in it, but Judas by his deed deserved the punishment of his destruction. "It had been good ... if he had never been born": an expression by way of illustration, and it carries a figure of the severity of this man's punishment, so that it would have been better for him not to be born than to be born and fall into this evil and sin, and deserve this terrible judgment.

paragraphs.text: After the supper of the lamb, the Lord took bread and blessed it, and it changed into His true Body in a transcendent, mystical manner, and He declared quite clearly that this bread had become His Body, "Take, eat: this is My body", and He presented and gave this Body to them to eat ... and therefore the Church has kept in her Divine Liturgy the same words that the Lord Christ uttered.
